item.title: STAFF POST OPEN - Crosslink Proposal
item.content:encoded:
The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

Show Reasoning
Hide Reasoning

Write a paragraph here stating what you are proposing to link to, and why. If people can see your logic, they are more likely to agree with it.

Editing this:

Instances that were successfully disassembled, then reassembled and detonated, did not display any anomalous properties.

AND

However, approximately 35-37 seconds following the detonation, a mass of plant life will rapidly grow to cover the majority of the damaged area

To this:

Instances that were successfully disassembled, then reassembled and detonated, did not display any anomalous properties. Some instances of SCP-540 have demonstrated anomalous properties related to other explosive SCPs, including SCP-2283.

AND

However, approximately 35-37 seconds following the detonation, a mass of plant life will rapidly grow1 to cover the majority of the damaged area

Footnotes
1. Rapid generation of life in this manner closely resembles the cyclical generation of life in SCP-3044.

I think connecting this with an explosive SCP is an obvious cool connection so I propose the following edit:

Instances that were successfully disassembled, then reassembled and detonated, did not display any anomalous properties. Some instances of SCP-540 have demonstrated anomalous properties related to other explosive SCPs, including SCP-2283.

item.content:encoded:
I'm… not sure what your complaint here is. Example:

Take 1001 randomly selected grenades and set 'em off without disassembling them first. 30 make plants.

Now take those same 100 grenades and, instead of setting 'em off immediately, disassemble them first. 50 would plant-splode, and the remaining 50 would be normal after being put back together.

Footnotes
1. Yes, ridiculously small sample size, but work with me here.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
However, instances of SCP-540 are indistinguishable from non-anomalous ordnance, …

Attempts to disassemble low-yield instances of SCP-540 for analysis have resulted in premature detonation and resultant plant growth in approximately 50% of all such attempts. Instances that were successfully disassembled, then reassembled and detonated, did not display any anomalous properties.

How do they know that the ones which don't prematurely detonate are non-anomalous, and the anomalous ones prematurely detonate 100% of the time?
